content:
Physiotherapy, also known as physical therapy, is a healthcare profession that focuses on the assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of physical impairments, functional limitations, and disabilities. The goal of physiotherapy is to enhance and restore functional ability and quality of life to those with physical impairments or disabilities. 

Physiotherapists, or physical therapists, use a variety of techniques to help patients recover from injuries, surgeries, or chronic conditions. These techniques can include exercises, manual therapy, education, and advice to promote movement, reduce pain, restore function, and prevent disability. They work with individuals of all ages and tailor treatment plans to meet the specific needs of each patient.

Physiotherapy can be beneficial in a wide range of settings, such as hospitals, private clinics, sports facilities, rehabilitation centers, and in-home care. Conditions commonly treated include musculoskeletal disorders, sports injuries, neurological conditions, cardiopulmonary issues, pediatric conditions, and geriatric concerns.
